To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PD‐L1 expression is heterogeneous within NSCLC samples, with higher PD‐L1 in squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) than in adenocarcinoma (ADC), (2) ADC samples are more likely to have PD‐L1 discordance, and (3) the discordance rate is 20% in ADC and 10% in SCC, with discordant samples more likely to be PD‐L1 positive.
PD‐L1 immunoreactivity was significantly higher in adenocarcinoma compared to squamous cell carcinoma and large cell carcinoma, with a trend towards higher PD‐L1 in small cell carcinoma.

intratumoral PD-L1 variation is associated (p = 0.001) with differences in local NSCLC histotype, and the most common discordant histotypes are squamous cell carcinoma (SCC)/adenocarcinoma (AC), SCC/small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) and AC/SCLC (each 12.5%).
In summary, our research is concerned with
PD‐L1 expression in NSCLC.
the heterogeneity of PD‐L1 immunoreactivity in NSCLC and the potential implications for clinical decision‐making.
the relationship between PD‐L1 immunoreactivity and histology in NSCLC.

PD‐L1 immunoreactivity varies between NSCLC histotypes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of intratumoral heterogeneities of PD‐L1 expression in NSCLC is associated with variation of local histotypes, and that this is a phenomenon that is not confined to squamous cell carcinoma.
the frequency of discordant PD‐L1 immunostaining between histotype areas is low, but the potential for discordance is greatest when the tumour has a squamous component.
intratumoral heterogeneities are common and are associated with differences in histotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intratumoral heterogeneities in PD‐L‐1 immunohistochemical staining are common, and may be related to differences in histotype.
